source_text: In principio fecit Deus coelum et terram. Quod est omnium principium nisi Dominus noster et Salvator omnium Iesus Christus, primogenitus omnis creaturae? In hoc ergo principio, hoc est in Verbo suo, Deus coelum et terram fecit, sicut Evangelista Iohannes ait: In principio erat Verbum. Non temporale aliquod principium dicit, sed in principio, id est in Salvatore, factum esse dicit coelum et terram. Terra autem erat invisibilis et incomposita, et tenebrae erant super abyssum, et spiritus Dei ferebatur super aquas.
pass_a_gloss: In beginning made God heaven and earth. What is of-all beginning unless Lord our and Savior of-all Jesus Christ, firstborn of-every creature? In this therefore beginning, this is in Word his, God heaven and earth made, as Evangelist John says: In beginning was Word. Not temporal some beginning he-says, but in beginning, that is in Savior, to-have-been-made he-says heaven and earth. Earth however was invisible and unordered, and darknesses were over abyss, and spirit of-God was-borne over waters.
pass_b_english: [[In the beginning God made heaven and earth >> Bible:Genesis 1:1]]. What is the beginning of all things if not our Lord and Savior of all, Jesus Christ, [[the firstborn of all creation >> Bible:Colossians 1:15]]? In this beginning, that is in his Word, God made heaven and earth, as the evangelist John says: [[In the beginning was the Word >> Bible:John 1:1]]. He does not mean some temporal beginning, but says that heaven and earth were made in the Beginning — that is, in the Savior. [[The earth was invisible and unordered, and darkness was over the abyss, and the Spirit of God was borne over the waters >> Bible:Genesis 1:2]].
